subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — GPU sizing & SLO checklist

Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — GPU sizing & SLO checklist

Thanks for the call this morning — great to meet the Streamlytics team. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the performance/availability targets you mentioned and the next steps for a focused Dedicated-capacity PoC. Please review and flag anything I missed.

Top-level targets you gave (confirm these are the ones we should validate in PoC):
- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency <= 150 ms for responses up to 512 tokens (streaming enabled)
- Throughput: ~200 requests/sec (average request ~256 tokens) sustained for business-hours traffic; burst to 350 rps for peak windows
- Concurrency: ~200 concurrent sessions with active KV cache per session
- Streaming: incremental token-by-token streaming required; application expects first-token <40 ms from request acceptance
- Availability: regional SLA target 99.9% for inference endpoints (we'll discuss HA topology)

Questions / missing inputs we need from you to size the Dedicated pool: 
1) Typical prompt + response token distribution (we have the sample set you shared; can you confirm mean/median token counts and 95th percentile?)
2) Acceptable cold-start penalty for long-tail models (do you need <1s cold-start?)
3) Any hard constraints on hardware type (must be H100 vs allowance for A100 or mixed pools?)
4) For streaming, do you have a required max client-side idle timeout for mid-stream pauses?

Our proposed next steps:
- Dev will follow up with GPU-level throughput estimates and a candidate Dedicated config (A100 vs H100 tradeoffs) — target within 24 hours.
- Streamlytics to confirm token distributions & legal/procurement contacts for PO timeline.
- Schedule 1-week PoC (canary) with reserved throughput to validate p95 latency under 200 rps.

I attached a sizing workbook (redwood-dedicated-sizing-20260112.xlsx) with the assumptions we used in the calcs; please add your numbers in the green columns.

Thanks,
Marissa

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — GPU sizing & SLO checklist

Thanks, Marissa — adding the engineering perspective below. High-level summaries first, followed by numbers and recommended PoC configuration.

Short answer: H100 (80GB) gives the best headroom for your SLOs, but mixed pools with A100 (40/80GB) can be cost-effective if you tune batching and KV cache behavior.

GPU comparison (practical implications):
- H100 80GB (best perf)
  - Pros: ~1.6–2x faster per-token generation vs A100 80GB for transformer decoder workloads with long context; better CUDA cores + Tensor-Core perf for FP16/TF32 kernels. Handles bigger batch sizes while keeping p95 low.
  - Cons: higher EC2 price; may be overprovisioned if you have short responses and low concurrency.
- A100 80GB / 40GB
  - Pros: cheaper per-hour; predictable performance, good for steady throughput with aggressive batching.
  - Cons: needs larger cluster to hit p95 at low latency for streaming-first workloads.

Estimated sizing (based on your targets: 200 rps, avg 256 tokens/request, streaming):
- H100-focused config (recommended for tight p95): 4 x H100-80GB nodes with continuous batching disabled for low latency but with adaptive micro-batching (target micro-batches of 4–8). This configuration estimates sustained throughput ~300 rps with p95 <150 ms for 512-token responses (subject to model choice & quantization).
- Mixed config (cost-optimized): 6 x A100-80GB nodes + 2 x H100 (for peak and long-context requests). Expected sustained throughput ~260 rps; p95 ~160–180 ms depending on workload skew.

Reserved throughput / capacity planning:
- For a PoC canary: request reserved throughput of 250 rps for the Dedicated pool (20% buffer). We'll instrument token-level telemetry and simulate realistic session concurrency and KV cache warming.
- For production commit: recommend initial reserve 200 rps with auto-burst to 350 rps (burst from a shared pool) and autoscaling policy during off-peak to avoid cost overruns.

Streaming specifics:
- First-token latency: with micro-batching and pinned model instances, we can achieve first-token <40 ms on H100 for typical prompts. A100 may see first-token ~50–80 ms depending on batching.
- KV cache: per-session KV is memory-bound; choose 80GB GPUs for safe cache residency for 2k token contexts per session.

Quantization & perf knobs:
- int8/4-bit quantization helps cost but can increase p95 variance. For PoC we recommend FP16/TF32 to validate SLOs, then try 8-bit to measure unit-cost savings.
- Enable prefix caching and aggressive cache TTL for repeated prompts to reduce token compute.

PoC plan (what we'll run):
1) Baseline run on one H100 node with production-like request distribution to capture cold/warm latency curves.
2) Dedicated cluster (4x H100) run for sustained 200 rps and burst tests to 350 rps. Collect p50/p95/p99 and token throughput.
3) Streaming validation: long-lived connections with intermittent token pauses to validate first-token and mid-stream recovery.

I'll attach a short benchmark summary (gpu-benchmark-summary.pdf) with the microbenchmarks we referenced; that should map to the workbook. Happy to run an initial smoke test this week if Streamlytics can grant us a narrow IP range for the PoC or run via your VPC peering.

—Dev
